headlines.title: 구윤철 " 개정 노조법 현장 안착 총력"…시행 초기 3개월 집중점검

headlines.title: 정부, 호르무즈 봉쇄에 중동 위기경보 발령

headlines.title: 가뜩이나 불안한 환율에 ‘ 기름 ’… 간밤 1500원대 뚫려
headlines.summary: 글로벌 자금 달러로 쏠려 한은 “現상황 과거와 달라” 4일 원·달러 환율이 17년 만에 ‘심리적 지지선’인 1500원 선을 넘어선 것은 이란의 호르무즈 해협 봉쇄에 따른 시장의 위기감을 단적으로 보여 준다는 평가다. 중동 지역의 군사적 충돌이 장기화 양상으로 흘러가면서 글로벌 자금이 달러로 쏠리는 반면 원화 약세 압력은 가중되고 있다.

headlines.title: 1500원 뚫린 환율 ... 중동 發 쇼크에 2% 성장 '흔들'
headlines.summary: 1500원을 뚫은 원화값은 수입물가 상승과 에너지 비용 증가로 이어지며 한국 경제에 즉각적인 타격을 줄 수 있다. 국제유가와 원·달러 환율 동시 급등은 각종 원자재 가격과 물류비용 등 생산원가 상승으로 이어지면서 소비자물가를 자극하는 다중 악재로 작용한다. 물가, 금리, 증시 전반을 흔드는 복합 리스크가 현실화했다는 우려도 나온다.

headlines.title: “ 유가·환율 상승땐 팔수록 손해 ” 중기 ‘ 원가 구조 ’ 먼저 무너진다 ...
headlines.summary: 국제유가 최고 130달러까지 ‘경고등’ 연료·원자재·해상운임 등 상승 압박 영업이익률 저조한 중기에 더 치명적 미국과 이란 간 군사 충돌이 격화됐다. 국제 유가는 하루 만에 6% 넘게 급등했다. 문제는 앞으로다. 호르무즈 해협이 전면 봉쇄될 경우 국제 유가는 배럴당 120~130달러까지 치솟을 수 있다는 전망까지 나왔다.

headlines.summary: 오늘장 미 증시 일제히 하락했습니다. 장 초반 보였던 낙폭을 일부 축소하긴 했지만 3대 지수 모두 1%가량 내렸고 러셀 2000 지수도 1. 7% 하락했으며 11개 섹터가 일제히 부진했습니다. 오늘도 시장의 눈은 중동 정세로 향했습니다. 가장 요동친 건 유가와 채권 시장이었습니다.

headlines.title: “ 호르무즈 해협 완전봉쇄 땐… 브렌트유 200달러 찍을 것”
headlines.summary: ■ IB들 유가시장 시나리오 분석 현재 배럴당 81.4달러 수준 사태 3주 지속 땐 강제 감산 가격 2.5배로 오를 가능성 미국·이스라엘의 공습 이후 이란 이슬람혁명수비대(IRGC)가 세계 최대 원유 수송로인 호르무즈 해협을 전면 봉쇄하겠다고 선언하면서 국제 유가가 요동을 치고 있다.

headlines.title: 트럼프 "세계 각국에 차등 관세 매길 것"…무역법 301조 등 적용 재확인

headlines.title: 증권가 비관적 전망 “ 전쟁 장기화 땐 코스피 30 % 하락 가능성”
headlines.summary: 코스피가 미국과 이란 간 전쟁 발발 여파로 역대 최대 폭으로 폭락해 5,100선마저 내준 4일 서울 중구 하나은행 본점 딜링룸에 코스피와 삼성전자, 하이닉스, 원/달러 환율이 표시돼 있다. 연합뉴스 미국의 이란 공습 이후 이틀 새 코스피가 18% 급락하면서 증권가가 ‘최악의 시나리오’ 분석을 내놓고 있다.

key_headlines.title: Government to Intensively Monitor Revised Labor Act's Implementation
key_headlines.summary: The government will operate an intensive 3-month monitoring period for the revised Labor Union Act (Yellow Envelope Law), set to take effect on March 10th, to ensure its stable establishment in workplaces.

key_headlines.title: Deputy PM Goo Pledges Efforts for Smooth Labor Law On-site Establishment
key_headlines.summary: Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Economy and Finance, Goo Yun-cheol, chaired a meeting, pledging all-out efforts for the revised Labor Union Act's smooth on-site establishment and continuous communication among labor, management, and government.

key_headlines.title: Deputy PM Goo Expresses Vigilance Over Surging Exchange Rate
key_headlines.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Goo Yun-cheol stated that the government is monitoring the won-dollar exchange rate with 'vigilance' following its rapid increase, acknowledging external shocks as a contributing factor.

key_headlines.title: Won-Dollar Rate Breaches 1500; Deputy PM Assures Ample Forex Reserves
key_headlines.summary: The won-dollar exchange rate temporarily exceeded 1500, prompting Deputy Prime Minister Goo Yun-cheol to assure the public that South Korea possesses ample foreign exchange reserves of $400 billion, with $1 trillion including private holdings, mitigating concerns of a dollar shortage.

key_headlines.title: Government Reviews Potential Impact of Revised Labor Act on Subcontracting
key_headlines.summary: The revised Labor Union Act, particularly articles 2 and 3, is seen as institutionalizing the possibility of co-negotiations for win-win outcomes in the original and subcontracting structure, marking a significant change in labor relations.

sections.Hot Economy News: The Korean government is set to implement the revised Labor Union Act, known as the 'Yellow Envelope Law,' on March 10th, initiating a three-month intensive monitoring period to ensure its stable on-site establishment. Deputy Prime Minister Goo Yun-cheol chaired a meeting, emphasizing the importance of continuous communication among labor, management, and government. Concurrently, Deputy PM Goo also expressed heightened vigilance over the rapidly increasing won-dollar exchange rate, which briefly surpassed 1500, attributing the surge partly to external shocks from the Middle East. He reassured the public that Korea's substantial foreign exchange reserves of over $400 billion, including private sector holdings of $1 trillion, are more than sufficient, mitigating any concerns of a dollar shortage.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: China has set its GDP growth target for 2026 at 4.5-5%, a slight reduction from previous years, while maintaining its unemployment target at 5.5% and consumer price inflation at around 2%. The country also announced a 7% increase in its defense budget, marking four consecutive years of such growth. Concurrently, the US Federal Reserve's latest Beige Book report indicated that economic activity generally maintained a modest expansion but noted an increase in regions experiencing economic slowdown and persistent inflationary pressures. These factors contribute to the speculation that the timing for interest rate cuts could be delayed, as also reflected in some companies passing on increased tariff costs to customers.
sections.Financial Markets: The Korean stock market experienced a significant rebound, with the KOSPI surging 9% and the KOSDAQ jumping 14%, recouping losses from previous days and signaling a recovery in investor sentiment. This rally was accompanied by a stabilization of the won-dollar exchange rate, which closed at 1468.1, down 8.1 won from the previous day, after briefly breaching the 1500 mark. Meanwhile, US Treasury bond yields rose for the third consecutive day amid renewed inflation concerns fueled by surging oil prices and growing panic over the Iran conflict. Market expectations for a 25bp rate cut at the June FOMC meeting have notably decreased to 35.5%, indicating a shift in monetary policy outlook.
sections.Industry & Technology: South Korea's battery industry is strategically expanding beyond electric vehicles (EVs) into robotics and Energy Storage Systems (ESS), following a challenging year marked by Chinese competition and reduced EV subsidies. LG Energy Solution, in particular, announced a breakthrough with its all-solid-state based sulfur cathode technology, demonstrating its potential for next-generation battery dominance even in pouch cell form factors applicable to EVs. The stock market saw significant gains in secondary battery, biopharmaceutical, semiconductor, and robot sectors, with several companies like EcoPro and Alteogen experiencing sharp increases. Separately, oil tanker shipping rates surged three-fold due to the Hormuz Strait closure, while domestic semiconductor production saw a decline, contributing to an overall decrease in industrial production for the first time in three months.
sections.Real Estate: The government is considering new regulations on 'non-resident single homeowner' jeonse (lump-sum deposit) loans, causing ripples in the financial and real estate sectors amid discussions to curb real estate speculation. While Seoul apartment price increases have slowed for five consecutive weeks, non-regulated areas in Southern Gyeonggi, such as Dongtan, are seeing price increases and high subscription rates. Furthermore, the proportion of new high-price transactions (신고가) in Seoul apartments decreased last month, particularly in Yongsan and Mapo districts, suggesting a cooling in previously leading areas. Amid rising jeonse prices, there's a noticeable shift towards 'ban-jeonse' (semi-monthly rent) contracts, where a lower deposit is paid along with a monthly rent, as the monthly rent ratio increased significantly.
sections.International Economy: The US Federal Reserve's latest Beige Book report indicated a modest economic expansion with increasing regional slowdowns and persistent inflation, also noting that some businesses continue to pass on tariff costs. Concurrently, US Treasury bond prices sharply declined amid 'Iran war panic,' pushing yields higher and reducing market expectations for a June interest rate cut. In a separate development, a US court ruled in favor of refunding 'Trump tariffs' on certain imports, while former President Trump officially nominated Kevin Warsh for Fed Chair, amidst ongoing scrutiny. There is also a warning from a US think tank that the US is considering using Trade Act Section 301 against countries implementing 'digital barriers,' such as Korea's proposed Online Platform Law.
sections.AI & Economy: The National AI Strategy Committee addressed growing concerns about AI's impact on employment, emphasizing that AI should be viewed not as a replacement technology but as a productivity-enhancing tool that enables people to perform safer and higher value-added tasks. This stance was articulated during the first 'Relay Dialogue on AI Transformation in the Labor Field and the Future of Jobs,' as AI technology's expansion into various industries transforms work methods and job structures. The committee aims to discuss adaptation challenges and necessary institutional improvements arising from these changes, promoting a balanced approach to AI integration in the economy.
sections.Others: Gyeonggi Province Governor Kim Dong-yeon ordered emergency support measures for small and medium-sized enterprises affected by the worsening Middle East situation, including assistance for increased logistics costs and additional export vouchers. The Ministry of Employment and Labor held a town hall meeting to gather opinions from youth on employment, labor environments, and income to reflect in next year's budget. The Korea Exchange announced that the 'Value-up Index' reached a record high in February, signaling strong market confidence in companies with enhanced corporate value. A US think tank warned that South Korea's proposed Online Platform Law could be seen as a digital trade barrier, potentially leading to trade retaliation under Section 301, while Intel Foundry is reportedly seeking customers for its 1.8nm process, targeting major US tech companies.
